claims.text: The target refractory HEA has coherent δ-lamellae and γ″ precipitates.
Retention of high toughness depends on maintaining a fine, coherent precipitate dispersion.
Increasing aging temperature or time promotes precipitate coarsening and loss of interfacial coherence.
Precipitate coarsening and loss of coherence degrade toughness.
Coarsening and loss of coherence cause dislocation slip to localize and shear δ-lamellae instead of producing distributed plasticity.
Aging temperature and time can be varied to tune precipitate size, distribution, and coherency.
Precipitate size and δ/γ″ interfacial coherency govern dislocation interactions and local shear distribution.
γ″ particles pin dislocations as dislocations cut through the δ-lamellae.
Coherent δ-lamellae permit planar dislocation slip and shearing across coherent δ/γ boundaries.
Slip bands shear the δ-lamellae and can produce approximately 40% local shear at 14% tensile strain.
Shearing of coherent δ-lamellae can alleviate local stress concentration rather than create a crack.
Fine, coherent precipitates promote distributed slip, delay crack initiation, and enhance toughness.
Coarsened, incoherent precipitates permit easier lamellar shearing and lead to localized shear bands.
Optimally aged samples will retain high toughness and show distributed dislocation slip with minimal local shear.
Optimized aging will avoid approximately 40% local shear.
Overaged samples will have lower toughness, more localized shear bands, and earlier crack initiation than the baseline.
The hypothesis is restricted to aging regimes that do not cause unwanted phase transformations and to representative service-loading conditions.
The quantitative aging–coherency–toughness relationship may depend on alloy composition and processing history.
The coarsening threshold at which toughness significantly degrades is not established.
The hypothesis would be falsified if substantial precipitate coarsening and coherence loss occurred without toughness decreasing relative to the baseline.

contradictions.description: The mechanism treats coherent-lamella shearing and planar slip as beneficial for stress redistribution, while the predicted outcome describes optimized samples as avoiding approximately 40% local shear. The cited 40% value actually refers to beneficial local shear in the coherent baseline, so the proposed observation is internally misaligned with the stated mechanism.
